target.name: ByteCodeInterpreter boolean materialisation (sub_080007B6, sub_080007CC)
target.role: replace the stack top with the flag bit, and with its inverse
target.notes: sub_080007B6 (22 bytes, 10 instructions) and sub_080007CC (26 bytes, 12 instructions), adjacent, one terminator each at 0x080007CA and 0x080007E4, one call each to the already-lifted reader sub_08004364, and one shared literal at 0x080008D8. THE DESTINATION IS THE SAME AT BOTH SITES, and it is derived rather than assumed: each computes its address as `context + count*4` from the counter at context+0x00 (`ldr r1,[r0] ; lsls r1,r1,#2 ; adds r4,r1,r0`), and the value stack holds values[i] at context + 4 + 4*i, so context + count*4 is context + 4 + 4*(count-1), which is values[count-1], THE TOP OF THE STACK. Both routines therefore REPLACE THE STACK TOP IN PLACE. This is NOT a pop: neither stores to context+0x00, so the COUNTER IS UNCHANGED, and it is not a separate word either. The two differ only in what they store: the first stores the flag (0 or 1), the second stores 1 - flag, so for a boolean input the second is the exact inverse of the first. Both return the value they stored in r0, and neither reads r1. THE STACK IS NOT CHECKED FOR BEING EMPTY: with a counter of zero the computed address is context + 0, so the word read is the COUNTER itself and the store REPLACES THE COUNTER with the flag, leaving the count at 0 or 1. No guard was added. THE FIRST CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE, proven through the already-lifted consumer sub_080007E6 which begins immediately after these two at 0x080007E6: it pops values[count-1] and passes it to sub_08004380, which sets bit (value & 7) of the byte at base + (value >> 3) + 0x55. With a materialised boolean the index is 0 or 1, so THE BOOLEAN SELECTS WHICH BIT IS SET in the first byte of the flag array - bit 0 when the tested flag was clear, bit 1 when it was set. The boolean is therefore used as a BIT INDEX by the first consumer downstream of it, not as a truth value. UNKNOWN: what either bit means, whether callers rely on the counter being untouched, and what reads the array afterwards. No semantic name is assigned, and nothing is imported from another title.

bool_materialisation.destination: values[count-1], the TOP of the VM value stack, replaced in place
bool_materialisation.counter_unchanged_evidence: neither routine stores to context+0x00; the only store in each is to the slot register computed from the counter
bool_materialisation.consequence: the already-lifted consumer sub_080007E6 pops the materialised 0/1 and passes it to sub_08004380 as the bit number, so the boolean SELECTS WHICH BIT is set in the flag array: bit 0 when the tested flag was clear, bit 1 when it was set
bool_materialisation.empty_stack_behaviour: with a counter of zero the address is context itself, so the counter word is read as the value and then REPLACED by the flag; nothing is popped and there is no check

verdicts_are_independent: SEMANTIC, MODERN_BUILD and ADS_MATCH answer different questions and none is evidence for another. A passing modern build says nothing about the original compiler; a passing semantic run only removes one class of error.

identity.why_not: the original translation unit was built by ARM Developer Suite 1.2 (the surviving command line names tcpp). GCC is a different compiler with a different code generator, so its output cannot establish anything about ADS 1.2.

literal_pools.interpretation: the original's literals are accounted for by the words the unit declares; the modern build pools differently, which is a structural consequence of the compiler rather than a defect in the reconstruction. It is also why a function with a literal load cannot be compared standalone.

comparison.match_claim_note: MEASUREMENT ONLY. This compares a modern GCC build against the cartridge. A modern compiler is not the original compiler, so a difference here is expected and proves nothing; an identity here would also prove nothing about ADS 1.2. ADS_MATCH stays BLOCKED.
